questions.q: What is the primary territorial dispute between India and Pakistan, and which UN resolution called for a plebiscite in the region?
questions.a: The primary dispute is over the erstwhile princely state of Jammu & Kashmir. UN Security Council Resolution 47 (1948) called for a plebiscite after Pakistani withdrawal and Indian force reduction — conditions never met. A wrong answer (e.g., "Sir Creek" or "Siachen" as primary, or citing Shimla Agreement for plebiscite) reveals confusion between core and peripheral disputes, and between UN and bilateral frameworks.

questions.q: Why has India's "No First Use" nuclear doctrine not prevented Pakistan from pursuing tactical nuclear weapons (TNWs), and what strategic instability does this create?
questions.a: Pakistan's TNWs (Nasr missile) aim to offset India's conventional superiority by lowering the nuclear threshold, betting India won't risk massive retaliation for a limited tactical strike. This creates "stability-instability paradox": nuclear deterrence at strategic level enables conventional/sub-conventional adventurism (e.g., Kargil, Mumbai attacks). A wrong answer focusing only on "Pakistan wants parity" misses the doctrinal asymmetry and the specific operational logic of TNWs.

questions.q: Analyse the 2020-2021 Galwan Valley clash in terms of: (a) the shift in LAC management protocols, (b) the role of infrastructure asymmetry, and (c) India's diplomatic-military response.
questions.a: (a) Galwan marked the first fatal clash since 1975, ending the 1993/1996 agreements' "peace and tranquillity" framework; (b) India's DS-DBO road construction reduced Chinese tactical advantage, triggering PLA's forward deployment; (c) India responded with forward deployment (50k+ troops), economic measures (app bans, FDI scrutiny), and Quad deepening — signalling cost imposition without escalation. A wrong answer treating it as "just another border skirmish" misses the paradigm shift in LAC management and India's calibrated escalation strategy.

questions.q: Compare the root causes and State responses to insurgency in Nagaland (NSCN-IM) versus Left-Wing Extremism in Chhattisgarh. Why did the Framework Agreement (2015) succeed politically where military offensives alone failed?
questions.a: Nagaland: ethnic identity, historical sovereignty claim → political negotiation (Framework Agreement 2015) recognising "unique history" without accepting sovereignty. LWE: governance vacuum, land alienation, tribal marginalisation → security-development mix (SAMADHAN doctrine: Smart leadership, Aggressive strategy, Motivation, Actionable intelligence, Dashboard KPIs, Harnessing technology, Action plan, No access to financing). Military-only approach fails both: Nagaland needed political accommodation; LWE needs development delivery. Wrong answer conflating them as "terrorism" misses the distinct political economies.

questions.q: Evaluate the effectiveness of India's "surgical strikes" (2016) and "Balakot airstrike" (2019) as deterrence signalling against Pakistan's proxy war. Consider escalation control, international signalling, and domestic political utility.
questions.a: Effective in: (1) signalling lowered tolerance threshold — crossing LoC/International Boundary; (2) domestic audience mobilisation; (3) forcing Pakistan to deny/obfuscate rather than retaliate conventionally. Limited in: (1) Pakistan's TNW doctrine unchanged; (2) proxy infrastructure (launchpads) rebuilt; (3) escalation risk high — Pakistan's 2019 retaliatory strike captured Abhinandan. Wrong answer claiming "permanent deterrence established" ignores Pakistan's strategic calculus: low-cost proxies vs. high-cost Indian retaliation remains favourable.

questions.q: Draft a 3-point "Internal Security Doctrine" for India that integrates: (i) political accommodation for identity-based insurgencies, (ii) development-security nexus for LWE, (iii) community policing for communal violence. Justify each point with a specific existing policy example.
questions.a: Good answer: (i) Political accommodation — extend Framework Agreement model to other Northeast groups (e.g., ULFA talks), using Article 371 special provisions as template; (ii) Development-security — scale up "Aspirational Districts Programme" in LWE areas with dedicated CAPF-development coordination cells (existing: SAMADHAN); (iii) Community policing — institutionalise "Mohalla Committees" (Mumbai model post-1993 riots) under Police Act amendments. Poor answer: generic "more forces, more development" without institutional design or citing actual mechanisms.
